IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Senate Committee on Natural Resources, Ocean & Recreation (originally sponsored by Senator Jacobsen)

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to aquatic lands; creating new sections;prescribing penalties; providing an expiration date; and declaring anemergency.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A city with a population of five hundredthousand or greater has sixty days from the effective date of thissection to negotiate a lease of aquatic lands with the department. Ifthe city fails to negotiate the lease of aquatic lands, the departmentof natural resources may impose the lease conditions of a county witha population of one million or greater.

The department of natural resources and thecity with a population of five hundred thousand or greater may utilizethe services of a mediator to ensure the successful negotiation of theleases referenced in this act.

A city with a population of five hundredthousand or greater may not be granted, nor may it spend, any aquatic p. 1 SSB 6535lands enhancement account funds until all leases referenced in this actare signed.
This act is necessary for the immediatepreservation of the public peace, health, or safety, or support of thestate government and its existing public institutions, and takes effectimmediately.
